cells.tense: Right now the pen fits your hand and the direction is picked cleanly.
cells.act: bear the next hour of it without deciding anything
cells.ask: When something lands heavy this week, carry it for an hour and decide nothing. At the end of the hour, see if you're still standing.
cells.core:
You can steer and you can carry, and the two aren't fighting right now. What you pick, you pick from clear sight — not from a shove you can't name and not from dread that showed up before you did. That's a rare pairing: a direction with weight behind it, and no white knuckles.

Where you're steady is under load. You hold what has to be held without hardening into stone, and that holding is what keeps the steering honest. When this is working, the pick and the load sit together — you choose a road you can actually stand under. So the practice isn't more force. Stay with a thing for an hour and decide nothing yet. Tiny, and harder than it sounds. One hour.
cells.sheetLine: You pick a direction you can stand under.
cells.verb: Saying this, not that, and holding to it
cells.place: Where you carry weight without going rigid under it

cells.tense: From where you sit, the future is being braced against before it happens.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: When you catch yourself forcing a result, stop and look at the whole thing you're inside — what's involved, who's involved, where you sit. Look until it shows you something you hadn't seen.
cells.core:
There's a grip in this. Results get shoved toward before their time, and the shove feels like strength when it's really bracing. You've left the moment behind and your arm is out, holding a shape the situation hasn't agreed to yet.

The trouble isn't that you can bear weight — it's that bearing has turned into pushing. When you take in the entire arrangement, not just the part you're squeezing, the pressure eases by itself. So next time you feel yourself forcing an outcome, look at the whole picture first and keep looking. Where you sit in it. What surrounds it. What you hadn't noticed. That loosens what a week of shoving won't.

cells.tense: The pen sits where it was set down and the room has gone quiet around it.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: For one day, do the ordinary things your own way — not the proper way, not for anyone watching. Make no case for it. Keep going anyway.
cells.core:
The weight nearby hasn't gotten lighter; the arms stopped lifting. Days run on momentum and the old answer of so what. Where you're standing, the steering has gone slack, and a long stretch of it has made the slack feel like Tuesday rather than a state.

The bearing hasn't left — it's uncharged, waiting. Pushing harder won't charge it. Doing things the way only you would do them will, with no audience and no case to make. Small, ordinary, today — and again tomorrow. Whatever that is for you, not to prove a point, just done and kept at it. That pulls the rest through.

cells.tense: A choice is being made this minute and it is dressed as routine.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Take one thing you'd call just how it's done — a task, a habit, a stance you didn't know you held — and claim it as yours. Then check if that holds.
cells.core:
Direction is being directed, and the hand on it isn't reporting in. Days go the way they go, and the line between what you picked and what you drifted into has gone soft. Nobody's steering wrong. It's that the steering stopped being visible, even to the one doing it.

Since drifting and picking look alike from here, claim one moment. Not a big one — the ordinary thing you do the same every week. Call it yours, name it as set by you. If that's true, nothing changes and something returns. If it isn't, the wheel is right there. Either way you're back at it.
cells.sheetLine: Direction is running on habit and calling it how things go.
cells.verb: Saying this, not that, and holding to it
cells.place: Where you carry weight without going rigid under it
